thread:
sarah.nguyen: Heads-up: getting a cluster of SSO anomalies — ~12 distinct users showing almost-simultaneous sessions with fast IP rotation and short-lived tokens. flagged by auth-anomaly rule.

infra-bot: alert: auth-anomaly v2 triggered (score 0.87) for 12 unique user_ids between 2024-11-12T02:12:03Z and 2024-11-12T02:14:10Z. top source IPs: 83.149.16.23, 45.77.12.9, 185.93.0.0/24 (rotating).

raj.chowdhury: can you paste a sample log line? looks like credential stuffing or session replay.

sarah.nguyen: sample: `sso_login user=ajensen@redwood.com provider=okta status=SUCCESS src_ip=83.149.16.23 ua="Mozilla/5.0" session_id=st_9f1a` then 30s later `sso_login user=ajensen@redwood.com provider=okta status=SUCCESS src_ip=45.77.12.9 session_id=st_9f1b` — different session ids but same short interval.

maria.lopez: Are these users in the same org/team? any service accounts?

sarah.nguyen: mix — 8 human user accounts, 4 service-ish (deploy hooks). Not seeing failed MFA attempts, MFA passed each time.

raj.chowdhury: MFA passing suggests session-level compromise or delegated tokens from an app. We should: 1) revoke active sessions for affected users, 2) block the rotating IP set at perimeter, 3) force revoke of any third-party app tokens for those users, 4) enable extra logging.

oncall-sre: ACK. I can run session revoke and IP block now. executing: `rbacctl sessions revoke --user-list /tmp/affected_users.txt --reason "suspected session replay"`

isaac.kim: Also add a temporary deny rule for `185.93.0.0/24` and `45.77.12.0/24` on the WAF while we triage. I'll push a network ACL for 1h.

maria.lopez: I'll open an incident page and notify Security SL. paging #sec-oncall and product security. we need to check any admin console access from those IPs.

raj.chowdhury: Good. Also check our Okta system logs for `token.exchange` events and any suspicious OAuth app grants. If an app is minting tokens, we need to revoke its client_id.

sarah.nguyen: quick runbook notes:
```
- Query auth logs: `select * from auth_events where src_ip in (...) and ts > '2024-11-12T02:00:00Z'`
- Revoke sessions: `rbacctl sessions revoke --user <user> --all-active`
- Revoke third-party grants in Okta for impacted users
- Rotate deploy hook secrets for affected service accounts
```

oncall-sre: Done: revoked sessions for the 12 users, pushed WAF deny for the 2 CIDRs for 60m. ticket: INC-2024-1112-01.

maria.lopez: I've notified legal and CISO. Setting severity to P2 until we confirm lateral access or data exfil. adding tasks: audit logs collection, search for admin API usage, check KMS access logs.

isaac.kim: KMS logs show no key usage from those IPs. good. but need to verify if any deploy hook rotated secrets after initial compromise.

raj.chowdhury: Next steps: 1) collect full auth event set, 2) investigate OAuth app tokens, 3) review client_id activity, 4) rotate any implicated creds, 5) create post-incident eval. Assigning owners: auth logs -> sarah; OAuth/apps -> raj; deploy hooks -> isaac.

sarah.nguyen: I'll push a set of filtered logs to the incident bucket and share a link.

maria.lopez: thanks. please paste checklist when done. short comms to internal teams: "We observed anomalous SSO activity for a small set of users. Sessions have been revoked and perimeter blocks applied. We are investigating and will update." :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: will keep monitor rule elevated for 24h and revert block if no further hits.

isaac.kim: leaving scanning on for similar session_id patterns across org. added regex watch for `st_[0-9a-f]{4}` weird churn.

raj.chowdhury: Agreed. After triage, let's schedule 1h postmortem tomorrow to decide controls: stricter app vetting, token lifetime reduction, and targeted RBAC audits.

maria.lopez: closing loop here for now — incident page live at /inc/INC-2024-1112-01. will update with findings.

sarah.nguyen: thanks all. if you see any unexpected admin console access, ping me immediately.

maria.lopez: FYI — added a follow-up task to check audit logging ingestion for gaps (KMS event forwarding + CloudTrail).

oncall-sre: monitoring.

isaac.kim: final: rotated deploy hook creds for 2 service accounts, confirmed no further activity in last 20m.

maria.lopez: updating severity -> P3 pending further evidence. we'll reopen if new hits appear. :white_check_mark:
